title: display
summary: Display a value with a MATLAB-style variable-name header.

gpu_support.notes: `display` is a side-effecting output sink. GPU-resident inputs are gathered to host memory before formatting, matching `disp`.

description: `display(X)` prints a MATLAB-style display block for `X`. When the callsite argument is a simple variable name, RunMat uses that name as the header; explicit expression arguments print only their value. For classdef objects, RunMat dispatches a registered `display` method first, then a registered `disp` method, before the generic formatter.
behaviors: An explicit `display(expr)` call prints the expression value without an `ans =` header.
Single-line values are printed on the same line as the header.
Multi-line values such as matrices, structs, tables, datetime arrays, duration arrays, and N-D pages are printed below the header.
Objects and handle objects dispatch a registered or inherited `display` method first, then an overloaded `disp` method, before generic formatting.
`display` exposes no output argument, and requesting one is an error.
limitations: RunMat does not yet implement the full `matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay` override protocol. Class-specific output currently requires a registered or inherited `display` or `disp` method.
Object-array display customization remains bounded by RunMat's current object-array and classdef infrastructure.
The generic fallback formatter is the same host-side formatter used by `disp`; unsupported object families fall back to their runtime summary string.

faqs.question: How is `display` different from `disp`?
faqs.answer: `disp(X)` prints only the value. `display(X)` prints a variable-name header such as `X =` before the value.

faqs.question: Does `display` support class-specific output?
faqs.answer: Yes. RunMat checks a registered `display` method first and then an overloaded `disp` method. The full `matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay` protocol is not yet modeled.

faqs.question: Does `display` gather GPU arrays?
faqs.answer: Yes. Like `disp`, `display` formats on the CPU and gathers provider-resident data through the active acceleration provider.

gpu_residency: `display` is a no-output sink. Provider-resident inputs are gathered to host memory for formatting.
gpu_behavior: `display` performs no provider kernel dispatch and is excluded from fusion planning.
Gather behavior is inherited from the same runtime gather path used by `disp`.
